//: What Next.js requires on top of the base, and nothing else. The App Router compiles every file as ESM and resolves imports the way a bundler does, so `module`, `moduleResolution` and `jsx` cannot stay as the base leaves them: `jsx: react-jsx` is the automatic runtime Next uses, and `nodenext` would make TypeScript read the `.tsx` files of a package without `"type": "module"` as CommonJS and refuse every `import` under `verbatimModuleSyntax`. `lib` gains the browser globals. Every strict flag of the base stays as it is. `paths`, `include` and `plugins` with a path are the consumer's: see the comment in base.json.
//next-does-not-rewrite-this: `next build` offers to write these same options into the tsconfig of the app, but it gives up as soon as the file has an `extends` — which is exactly what apps/web has. The values below are therefore the only ones in play, and a build never edits a committed file.
